lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: the correlation coefficient, slope and intercept in context, and correlation versus causation
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: the correlation coefficient, slope and intercept in context, and correlation versus causation

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 24 yes, 9 no; row 2: 25 yes, 25 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 4x + 11, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 4 test points.
Each additional test points is associated with 4 more hour studieds.
The predicted value is 4 test points when x is 0.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 4 test points.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Towns with more fire engines report more fire damage. What conclusion is justified?
choices: A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.

items.prompt: A data set records 39, 21, 14, 36, 39, 21, 30. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 28.57, median 29
mean 28.57, median 30
mean 30, median 28.57
mean 29, median 30

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 297 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 28 yes, 22 no; row 2: 42 yes, 33 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?
A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 5x + 24, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: The predicted value is 5 test points when x is 0.
Each additional test points is associated with 5 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 5 test points.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 5 test points.

items.prompt: In a randomised trial, one group received a tutoring programme and scored higher on average than the control group. What conclusion is justified?
choices: A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: A data set records 21, 4, 36, 5, 37, 34, 19. Give the mean and the median.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
